A linter is a Nim module that declares one or more checks and exports a linter value. It lives in your repository, next to the config that uses it.

A minimal linter

This is an example linter from the tests:

import std/strutils

import compiler/ast

import lint

#startSettings
type
  VarNamesSettings* = object
    minLength*: int = 3
    maxLength*: int = 12

  ConstNamesSettings* = object
    prefix*: string = "k"
#endSettings

proc runVarNames(ast: PNode, s: VarNamesSettings): seq[Finding] =
  for node in ast.sons:
    if node.kind == nkVarSection:
      for def in node.sons:
        if def[0].kind != nkIdent:
          continue
        let name = def[0].ident.s

        if name == "killTheLinter":
          raise newException(ValueError, "There is a bug in this check")

        if name.len < s.minLength:
          result.add def[0].toFinding(
            "variable `" & name & "` is shorter than " & $s.minLength & " characters"
          )
        elif name.len > s.maxLength:
          result.add def[0].toFinding(
            "variable `" & name & "` is longer than " & $s.maxLength & " characters"
          )

proc runConstNames(ast: PNode, s: ConstNamesSettings): seq[Finding] =
  if s.prefix.len == 0:
    return
  for node in ast.sons:
    if node.kind == nkConstSection:
      for def in node.sons:
        if def[0].kind != nkIdent:
          continue
        let name = def[0].ident.s
        if not name.startsWith(s.prefix):
          result.add def[0].toFinding(
            "constant `" & name & "` should start with `" & s.prefix & "`"
          )

let
  nameLinter* = Linter(name: "nameLinter")
  varNames* = nameLinter.addCheck("varNames", runVarNames)
  constNames* = nameLinter.addCheck("constNames", runConstNames)

Three things make this a linter:

  • a settings type, which may be empty
  • a proc taking the file's AST and the settings, returning a sequence of types: Finding
  • a types: Linter value and one types: Check per rule, created with types: addCheck

The AST

Checks receive the parsed file as a PNode from Nim's own compiler AST module (compiler/ast). Lint neither converts the tree nor provides a tree type of its own: the node a check walks is exactly the node the parser produced.

Writing a check therefore means importing compiler/ast and matching on node kinds. A check must not modify the tree: the same AST is shared by every step that runs against the file.

The compiler sources on the search path

compiler/ast ships with the Nim distribution rather than with Lint, so the compiler sources have to be on the search path. This affects both files you write:

  • the linter, because it imports compiler/ast to walk the tree
  • the config, because it imports lint, which imports compiler/ast in turn

Without it, neither compiles:

Error: cannot open file: compiler/ast

The fix is a one-line .nims file next to each of them:

--path:"$nim/"
What you haveWhere the file goes
A single-module linter foo.nimfoo.nims, next to it
A linter packaged as a Nimble packageconfig.nims in the package root
Your config linter.nimlinter.nims, next to it

Lint's own src/lint.nims contains the same line, which is why the library compiles when you install it.

Findings

A types: Finding carries a position and a message, and nothing else.

A check does not know the file it runs against, the linter it belongs to, or the severity its findings are reported with. The runner attaches all of that when it collects findings, which is what lets the same check run at different severities in different steps.

Use types: toFinding to build one from an AST node; it extracts the position from the node.

Settings

Settings are a plain object. Give each field a default in the type definition, and a config that omits the settings: block gets those defaults:

type
  VarNamesSettings* = object
    minLength*: int = 3
    maxLength*: int = 12

  ConstNamesSettings* = object
    prefix*: string = "k"

A config that does provide settings has its keys checked against this type, so a misspelled key is a compile error.

Using the linter

Import it from the config and refer to the checks by name:

import lint
import namelinter

runLint:
#startGlobalConfig
  sources = ["./src"]
  ignoredPatterns = ["./src/skip/skipped.nim", "./src/skip2/**/*"]
#endGlobalConfig

#startStepConfig
  step "Check naming":
    linter = nameLinter
    ignoredPatterns = ["./src/skip/skipped2.nim"]
    check varNames:
      severity = hint
      settings:
        minLength = 3
        maxLength = 12
    check constNames:
      severity = error
      settings:
        prefix = "k"
#endStepConfig
Note: The import must be a plain import a/b line for the GitHub Action to notice changes to the linter and rebuild the cached binary.
